insights.insight: The protocol has confirmed $1.09M in cryptographically verified GMV across 17,650 receipts — deterministic proof of purchase, not probabilistic inference. For brands paying $5+ CPM to guess at purchase intent, this is a structurally different signal class.

DKIM-verified receipts tied to 10 email vendors and 29 active metros provide post-purchase confirmation that no cookie or pixel can replicate. The targeting signal arrives after the transaction closes, not before it might.

SaaS subscriptions entered the receipt corpus on April 9, and Google appeared in the 14-day top brands list on April 28 — signaling the protocol is capturing digital commerce, not just grocery and big-box. Brand marketers in non-physical categories now have a verifiable footprint here.

The network peaked at 29 active CBSAs on April 19 and recorded an 11-CBSA single-heartbeat burst on May 1 — the largest geographic burst in observation history. Diffusion is uneven and burst-driven, which matters for regional campaign planning.

7-day GMV has contracted 63.5% from its $210K peak to a $66K–$85K operating band, and token acceleration crossed below 1.0x for the first time on May 1, confirmed across two consecutive readings. Growth is plateauing; the dataset is maturing, not collapsing — but brands should size expectations accordingly.

Receipt submission peaks consistently in the 16:15–20:15 window and troughs at 00:15 overnight rolloffs — a stable, repeatable cycle across at least three days of observation. Brands running time-sensitive verification campaigns can align activation windows to this submission rhythm.
